rationale: Spec alignment: pass. The corrected M1 preserves the approved direct TestCase/behavior-module composition and now implements the required factory/resource/assertion responsibility split. Each formerly compound assertion consumer explicitly invokes run_validator or the Project Map component operation. Dynamic scenarios acquire a TemporaryDirectory, create/copy the owned input, apply the defining fault and execute the operation within that visible lifecycle. assert_validation_passes, assert_validation_fails and assert_contract_errors receive observed results and independent expected diagnostics only. TEST-SR-19/20 and the approved dependency graph are satisfied without changing product behavior or introducing a framework.

Test coverage: pass. Metadata's 23 cases retain valid inputs and exact intended metadata/readability rejections; Resource Map's 23 retain COPY/READ/RUN classes, absent resources, traversal/absolute paths and instruction-boundary alternatives; Assets' 31 retain metadata, placeholders, exact skeleton/field expectations, forbidden policy additions and generated/adapter presence observations. Their independently written expected messages and supplied invalid inputs still detect the intended failures. None is retired or consolidated merely to reduce size; relocated scenarios are retained, and the corrected helper roles make the tested action visible.

Test coverage, remaining M1 groups: pass for preservation. Canonical guidance's 32 and inherited guidance's 3 preserve structural drift guards for cross-skill contracts and maintain their explicit nonsemantic claim; installed placement's 9 retain compliant and missing/wrong recording/navigation inputs; portability's 6 retain controlled detector examples plus current published surface checks; Project Map's 12 retain controlled contract fixtures, canonical-copy faults, representative outputs and ownership checks; CI input's 8 retain the real canonical validator and individually mutated schema/resource/risk/review/repair conditions; CLI's 4 retain actual subprocess observations for acceptance, runtime independence, missing-target failure and multiple targets. These are justified retained protections at their actual observations; no structural text check is promoted to semantic skill approval and no generated-presence check is promoted to packed installation proof.

Edge cases: pass. The correction preserves all 97 test names in the five affected scenario modules. Independent read-only AST/source comparison against the hash-matched first subject preserved 39 fixed-fixture invocation/diagnostic pairs, 14 defining mutation/diagnostic pairs, 13 dynamic resource invocations and the effective configurations of all 23 resource scenarios; every nested mutate body is unchanged. Seven builder/operation functions remain AST-identical. These checks corroborate the independently inspected diff, including exact failure messages, COPY/READ/RUN variations, absolute/traversing paths and canonical/controlled Project Map diagnostic subjects. First-pass unchanged-case and named-parameter protection remains applicable where its exact subjects and relevant dependencies are unchanged.

Error handling: pass. Pure command assertions still check the expected exit condition and independently supplied diagnostic in captured stdout/stderr; error-list assertions require a nonempty result and intended message. The caller observes the operation exactly once, and TemporaryDirectory encompasses input creation, mutation, validation and assertion so cleanup remains exception-safe. No expected failure is turned into success, no fake replaces an existing real observation, and no defining fault moves into a hidden preset.

Architecture boundaries: pass. The ten direct groups retain metadata, resources, assets, installed placement, portability, Project Map, CI input, canonical guidance, CLI and general guidance ownership. The fixture helper no longer imports a consuming test module or invokes a command from an assertion. Fresh builders, the explicit Project Map operation helper and pure invariant assertions may share that small module while retaining distinct responsibilities. Temporary resources stay owned by the cases. Shared guidance assertions remain bounded. No deeper inheritance or global mutable fixture state is introduced.

Compatibility: pass. The aggregate continues ordinary unittest collection with each class imported once and no alias/load_tests workaround. The author supplied exact old-to-new mapping: every method moved to these ten classes previously collected as SkillValidatorFixtureTests.<same method>. Actual source/catalog caller inspection found no runtime consumer of the old mixed class; existing aggregate invocation remains supported. The ten new paths are classified with the existing Skill and adapter consumers, and the existing routing regression now checks each path against those independent expected checks. The contributor link points to the owning Design rather than a duplicate standard.

Security/privacy: pass within this source-only test refactor. Product authorization, external service use, package/runtime dependencies, secrets and release behavior are unchanged. Private temporary paths and subprocess text capture retain existing behavior. No credentials, network operation, destructive cleanup, production fallback or new authority are introduced in the changed code.

Derived artifact currency: pass within the affected scope. No canonical skill, schema, template or generated adapter is authored in M1, and no generated source edit is smuggled into the change. Existing asset and adapter observations remain test obligations. The inspected selected-CI log includes the affected adapter regression consumer. This review does not claim global packed, installed or released artifact currency.

Unrelated changes: pass. The source diff stays inside M1's mixed Skill class/support extraction and immediately necessary discovery/selection/contributor reconciliation. Other aggregate classes retain their bodies and discovery. The ExplicitRecordingGuidanceTests comment now states its existing structural guard and independent review limit without weakening an assertion. The still-large canonical behavior module is not independently disqualifying: the approved contract has no line-count target.
